title: Integrated AI and Wireless for Sustainable Mobile Network Evolutions
summary: The Venus team at Shanghai University proposes an AI application that predicts ionospheric delay in real time and reports no measured gain in positioning or communication.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The Venus project at Shanghai University combines wireless infrastructure with AI functions. One of these functions predicts ionospheric delay in real time. Ionospheric delay can affect the propagation of radio signals and positioning. In version 2 of a preprint, dated 15 April 2025, the Venus team reports the throughput and speedups of its wireless baseband processing chip, including a link-level throughput of 288 Mbps with a 45-core configuration. That paper says nothing about ionospheric delay prediction. The team's ITU entry, current as of June 2025, also describes separate gains from the chip, the compiler, and open-source infrastructure. The entry attributes none of these gains to the prediction system. No source quantifies an improvement in positioning or communication quality. ITU republished the same text in its final report of October 2025. No later source reports results for the ionospheric delay prediction.
purpose: Predict ionospheric delay in real time to support communications and positioning.
